t: The Ming dynasty restored Han Chinese rule in 1368 after driving the Mongol Yuan court back to the steppe.
Its examination-based bureaucracy, Zheng He's voyages and global silver trade made it a centre of the early modern world.
Fiscal crisis, famine and rebellion let Li Zicheng take Beijing in 1644, opening the way for the Manchu Qing.
dyk: The Ming Great Wall seen by visitors today is largely a 16th-century brick-faced work, built after the Zhengtong Emperor was captured by the Oirats at Tumu in 1449.
ev: Zhu Yuanzhang defeats Chen Youliang at the naval battle of Lake Poyang
Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming dynasty and his armies take the Yuan capital, Dadu
Zheng He's first expedition sets out on voyages that reach East Africa by 1433
The Forbidden City is completed in the Yongle Emperor's new capital, Beijing
The Oirat Mongols capture the Zhengtong Emperor at Tumu
The Ming intervene in Korea against the Japanese invasions
Li Zicheng takes Beijing; the Chongzhen Emperor takes his own life and the Qing occupy the city
The last Southern Ming loyalist regime comes to an end
